samples.summary: No test that `removeMember` purges nothing when the server refuses the removal, although the parallel case exists for `deleteWorkspace`

samples.summary: The `DurabilityLapse` publication path is untested end to end — only the pure `tooltipFor` is called with a hand-supplied lapse

finding.summary: The "Save a copy" recovery action is never exercised — the entire onClick hand-off is untested
finding.evidence: `offerRecoverableWork` builds a toast whose `action.onClick` calls `recoverOfflineCopy(store, item, { title, type })`, then branches on `outcome.refused` ('empty' / 'unsupported-type' / unreadable), on `outcome.complete`, and navigates via `getDocumentPath({ id: outcome.documentId!, type })`. `offline-runtime.test.tsx` only ever asserts the *negative*: `expect(recoverOfflineCopy).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` (line 179) and that the warning description contains the title. No test invokes `toastWarning.mock.calls[0][1].action.onClick`, so the argument wiring, all three refusal messages, the incomplete-copy notice and the Open/navigate path could all be broken and every suite would stay green. This is the path a user takes to get back work the SDK already gave up on — the payoff of the whole feature.

verdict.reason: The claimed-missing coverage exists in the same file the reviewer says they read in full. `offline-runtime.test.tsx` lines 208-316 contain a `describe('accepting the offer')` block whose `clickSaveACopy()` helper (lines 215-225) reads `toastWarning.mock.calls[0][1]`, asserts the action label is 'Save a copy', and calls `options.action.onClick()` (line 224). From there each branch the finding names is asserted: argument wiring to `recoverOfflineCopy` (store, item `{id:1,docKey:'sheet-7'}`, meta `{title:'Budget',type:'sheet'}`) at lines 227-242; the Open/navigate path by invoking the success toast's `action.onClick()` and asserting `navigate` received '/s/new-1' at lines 244-258 (with `getDocumentPath` NOT mocked — the vi.mock list at lines 20-87 does not include it, so the real path builder runs); the incomplete-copy notice at lines 260-275 plus the complementary `description` undefined assertion at line 254; and all three refusal messages ('empty', 'unsupported-type', undefined/unreadable) via `it.each` at lines 277-305, which additionally assert no success toast and no navigation. A throwing recovery is covered at lines 307-315. The `expect(recoverOfflineCopy).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` at line 189 cited as the sole evidence is a separate test asserting the offer does not auto-recover, not the extent of coverage; the `beforeEach` reset of `recoverOfflineCopy.mockResolvedValue` at lines 98-102 exists precisely to serve the click tests. The absence claim is factually false.

finding.summary: Nothing tests that PrivateRoute mounts OfflineRuntime, and every housekeeping promise depends on it
finding.evidence: `<OfflineRuntime userId={String(me.id)} />` is added inside `YorkieProvider` in `PrivateRoute.tsx`, and `offline-runtime.tsx`'s own header states this is "the only place that has both an identity and a lifetime longer than a single document". `grep -l 'PrivateRoute|OfflineRuntime'` matches only App.tsx, PrivateRoute.tsx, PublicRoute.tsx, README.md, offline-runtime.{tsx,test.tsx} and unrelated files — there is no PrivateRoute test anywhere. If this line were dropped or the id passed wrong, `rememberOfflineUser` never runs, so `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout()` finds no identity and silently erases nothing: document content stays on a shared device after sign-out, which is the exact promise the Settings copy makes. The OfflineRuntime unit tests all render the component directly and cannot catch this.

verdict.reason: A dedicated PrivateRoute test exists at packages/frontend/src/components/__tests__/private-route.test.tsx (kebab-case, which is why the reviewer's `**/PrivateRoute*` glob missed it). It covers exactly the behavior claimed untested: (1) it renders PrivateRoute through a MemoryRouter with fetchMe resolving {id: 42} and asserts offlineMounts[0] equals { userId: "42" } (lines 64-74) — this fails both if the `<OfflineRuntime userId={String(me.id)} />` line at PrivateRoute.tsx:35 is dropped and if the id is passed as a number instead of a string, the exact "id passed wrong" scenario cited; (2) it asserts the runtime is mounted inside YorkieProvider alongside the Outlet (lines 76-84); (3) it asserts nothing is mounted for an unauthenticated visitor who is redirected to /login (lines 86-95). The test is not vacuous: PrivateRoute itself is not mocked, only its collaborators, and the assertions observe props actually passed by the component's real render logic. It is wired in: vite.config.ts:452-457 includes src/**/*.test.tsx, and vite.config.ts:381 aliases "@" to ./src, so the vi.mock("@/components/offline-runtime") in the test resolves to the same module id as PrivateRoute.tsx:7's "./components/offline-runtime" import, meaning the mock genuinely intercepts the real import.

finding.summary: Newly exported `isOfflineUser` has no test; it is mocked at its only call site
finding.evidence: `isOfflineUser` is exported from offline-erase.ts and read by `removeMember` in api/workspaces.ts:159 to decide whether to purge with `{ dropArchives: true }`. `grep isOfflineUser` over packages/frontend finds it only in offline-erase.ts, workspaces.ts, and workspaces.test.ts — where it is `vi.fn()` mocked. `offline-erase.test.ts` imports eraseOfflineData, eraseOfflineDataOnLogout, purgeOfflineDocuments, purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments, rememberOfflineUser, retryPendingOfflineErase and watchForOfflineDisable, but not `isOfflineUser`. Its real behaviour (in-memory identity, localStorage mirror fallback, string vs number id) is therefore unexercised. A false positive here makes an owner removing *somebody else* purge this user's entries and drop their archives — the only copy of unreconciled work — while a false negative silently leaves a removed member's copies in place.

verdict.reason: The claim that `isOfflineUser` has no test is false in this working tree. `packages/frontend/src/lib/offline-erase.test.ts` imports `isOfflineUser` directly from `./offline-erase` (line 7, alongside `isOfflineWritePermitted` — the reviewer's quoted import list is incomplete) and exercises it against the real implementation in a dedicated `describe("whose documents this device holds")` block (lines 522–553). The tests are substantive, not vacuous: they assert the positive/negative discrimination for the signed-in account (`isOfflineUser("who-1")` true vs `isOfflineUser("who-2")` false, lines 528–533) — exactly the "removing somebody else must not purge this user's copies" behavior the finding says is unexercised — that it returns false once `rememberOfflineUser(undefined)` clears identity (lines 535–540), and that the localStorage mirror `wafflebase-offline-user` is written and cleared (lines 542–552), covering the fallback path in `offlineUserId()` (offline-erase.ts:90–99). Nothing in this file mocks `offline-erase`; the mock at `api/workspaces.test.ts:15` is a separate unit-boundary test of `removeMember`, and the module's own behavior is covered here. The only sliver not directly asserted is a numeric id, but the production call site coerces with `String(userId)` (workspaces.ts:159), so the string-keyed tests cover the values `isOfflineUser` actually receives.

finding.summary: `isPersistenceEnabled: getOfflinePersistenceEnabled` wiring into the store is untested, so nothing catches a regression that re-writes documents to the disk the user just cleared
finding.evidence: `DurableYorkieProvider` builds the store with `isPersistenceEnabled: getOfflinePersistenceEnabled`, and the comment says it is what stops the still-mounted client putting the open document back on the disk after the toggle is switched off. In `durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx` `WafflebaseDocStore` is entirely mocked (`captured.push(options)`), and the only option ever read back is `captured[0].onWriteFailure`; nothing asserts `isPersistenceEnabled`. In `collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx` the store is real and `isOpenElsewhere` IS proven (spy on `session.isOpenInAnyTab`), but `isPersistenceEnabled` is never probed (grep for `isPersistenceEnabled` in `*.test.*` matches only `wafflebase-doc-store-cleanup.test.ts`, which constructs its own store with its own option). So the store-level refusal is tested and the wiring that activates it is not.

verdict.reason: The finding claims `isPersistenceEnabled` wiring is untested and that in durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx "the only option ever read back is captured[0].onWriteFailure". That is false in this repository. The named test file contains a dedicated describe block, 'what the store is allowed to write' (lines 116-165), that captures and exercises the predicate: line 16 declares isPersistenceEnabled in CapturedOptions so it is read back; the test at lines 124-136 asserts captured[0].isPersistenceEnabled?.() === true at mount, flips the mocked preference to false WITHOUT re-rendering (line 133, the exact still-mounted scenario the finding describes), and asserts the predicate now returns false (line 135). A second test (lines 138-151) isolates the sign-out term by pinning offlineEnabled() to true (line 148) and asserting the predicate goes false via isOfflineWritePermitted. The assertions are non-vacuous: the predicate under test is the real production closure from durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:172-173 (only its two dependencies are mocked), so removing the option makes the call return undefined and fail line 127, dropping the preference term fails line 135, and dropping the permission term fails line 149. Glob confirms only one durable-yorkie-provider test file exists, so no stale/shadowing copy explains the reviewer's empty grep. One counterexample suffices for an absence claim, and there are three assertions.

finding.evidence: The diff adds a whole new Settings section: `offlineAvailable = supportsClientKey()` gating the section's existence, plus a `Switch` bound to `useOfflinePersistenceEnabled()` / `setOfflinePersistenceEnabled`. There is no test file for `app/settings/page.tsx` (glob `packages/frontend/**/settings*` finds no test; grep -i 'settings' over `*.test.*` in packages/frontend returns only unrelated files — workspace-settings, date-format-preference, etc.). The chip's equivalent gate IS tested ('offers nothing on a build that could not honour it'); the Settings one is not. A regression here presents a control promising per-device storage and erasure that the build cannot perform.

verdict.reason: A dedicated test for the Settings offline section exists at packages/frontend/tests/app/settings-offline.test.tsx, outside the src/ tree the reviewer searched. It renders the real Settings page (line 26 imports ../../src/app/settings/page) and asserts the supportsClientKey() gate in both directions: with the capability true the "Offline" heading and "Save documents on this device" switch are present (lines 43-49), and with supportsClientKey mocked false both are asserted absent (lines 51-60) — precisely the `offlineAvailable && (...)` gate at page.tsx:111 that the finding calls unasserted. The Switch binding is also covered: clicking it writes through the real preference module and flips aria-checked (lines 62-73), and a preference set by another surface is reflected on render (lines 75-87), exercising useOfflinePersistenceEnabled()/setOfflinePersistenceEnabled at page.tsx:32 and page.tsx:128. The "per device / turning it off deletes" copy is asserted at lines 89-97. Only the build-time capability module is mocked; the component under test is real, so inverting the gate would fail the test. The file is executed by the runner via the tests/**/*.test.tsx include in vite.config.ts:452-457. The absence claim is therefore false.
